summary: Keep II mtarakle/mtarək and III matrakle/matrək distinct as printed, though both mean aufgeben. Vowel placement and the m- are morphological evidence; semantics alone cannot choose the stem.

The solitary kturki supports a proposed I row, with its attested plural Infectum stated explicitly. The singular Infectum and Preterit base forms cannot be determined from this packet and are left open.
Object coding includes overt zero-marked nouns, fronted custom resumed by a feminine suffix, and a relative place indexed by -o. Preterit can have an overt l-marked agent (lu muxtar; lu paša).
The femo + m- collocation also occurs with rfy in the supplied glossary. This is evidence of a shared body-part construction, not proof of a particular contact origin or unrestricted synonymy.

The 33/53 entry example is structurally split across the wrong language fields. The two exact-span corrections restore the assigned source verse and its German translation without adding another copy.
Confirm whether Midyat kturki is productive stem I or exceptional reduction of an m-prefixed form. What are its base forms? Only the attested plural Infectum is supplied here.
Confirm the syntax of latyo ... d̥ḥa mtarakle in MAC Hanna Dewo/23: the Preterit-shaped verb occurs in an ought-not frame, not an asserted past event.
Do II and III abandonment differ by dialect, register or argument selection? The small sample does not establish a semantic contrast.
Abandonment applies to language as well as custom. The negative modal frame with Preterit-shaped mtarakle does not assert an earlier completed loss of the language.
Office, a hometown, cattle-herding and criminal activity are relinquishable objects. These participant domains do not require separate senses.
